blocks.content: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article 280 of the Constitution as a quasi-judicial body.

items: Qualifications of Finance Commission members are specified by Parliament by law, not directly detailed in the Constitution.
Recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory in nature and not legally binding on the executive.
Article 280 covers the establishment of the Finance Commission, whereas Article 281 deals with the recommendations of the Finance Commission.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Finance Commission is established under Article 280 of the Constitution as a quasi-judicial body to ensure financial devolution.
Members are appointed by the President of India, with qualifications and selection criteria defined by Parliament through the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951.
The Commission enjoys independence through constitutional status and quasi-judicial powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Its recommendations are submitted to the President, who presents them before both Houses of Parliament along with an explanatory memorandum.
While recommendations are advisory in nature, constitutional conventions ensure their substantial acceptance by the Union Government.
